SEATS FOR NON-PERMANENT
MEMBERS

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINA INCLUDED:

label: text
text: It has been decided that seats on the Council of the League will be allotted to Belgium, Sweden, Romania, Poland, China, Chile, Cuba or Columbia, Uruguay, and possibly Finland.

label: text
text: Belgium, Uruguay, and Sweden will be re-elected for one year; Romania, Chile, and Cuba or Columbia for two years; China and Poland, three years; and possibly Finland one year.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Genevi, Sept. 13.

label: text
text: The original scheme for the election of non-permanent members of the Council has been modified so that in the event of the resignation of a member there will be a by-election, whilst, re-eligibility will be decided separately by a secret bullet. Any member may ask the Assembly to direct that there be no discussion for re-eligibility.

label: text
text: Elections to the nine non-permanent seats will be held simultaneously.

label: text
text: The Business Committee of the Assembly will decide the procedure for fixing the number of years for a country's tenure of office—whether three years, two years, or one year.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: I'enque's Budget.

label: text
text: The Budget of the League, including the Labour Office and the International Court of Justice estimates that the expenditure for 1927 will be 24,615,000 Swiss francs—an increase of 1,700,000 francs over the current year.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
Riga, Sept. 13.
The Soviet newspapers are most dissatisfied with Germany's entry into the League. The Izvestia deplores her action in "joining a wasps nest of international intriguers where noguish diplomats are organizing a campaign against the Soviet Government." It concludes with the hope, however, that Germany will remain friendly to Soviet Russia.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: IN BANDITS' HANDS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
MEXICANS SEIZE RICH
AMERICAN

label: paragraph_title
text: CAR HELD UP

label: text
text: Mexico City, Sept. 13. Federal soldiers are pursuing bandits who are holding as prisoner Mr. Jacob Rosenthal, a retired New York merchant, after holding up a chair in which he was motoring with a party (including three other Americans) 40 miles from Mexico City as the party was returning from the sensible resort of Cuernayaca.

label: text
text: The bandits levelled their rifles, ordered the car to stop, took all the money and jewels, seized Rosenthal and dragged him into the neighbouring woods.

label: text
text: The curious fact is that no ransom is demanded, and the authorities are puzzled to know why Rosenthal was specially selected as prisoner.—Reuter's American Service

label: paragraph_title
text: CINEMA BLAZE.

label: paragraph_title
text: TALE OF A LIGHTED CANDLE.

label: paragraph_title
text: MANSLAUGHTER CHARGES.

label: text
text: At the inquest at Drumcolloghër on the bodies of the victims of the disaster in the cinema a verdict of death by asphyxiation by burning caused by a lighted candle falling on exposed films was returned. The jury found the operator guilty of negligence in leaving the films exposed and there was also carelessness on the part of the promoter in leaving a lighted candle on the table.

label: text
text: After the inquest the Civic Guards detained the promoter, Forde. and the operator Downing. —Reuter.

label: text
text:

manded in custody on a charge of
manslaughter.—Router

text: LONGEST TUBE.

label: text
text: À GERMAN DELEGATION.

label: text
text: The extension of one of London's tube, railways was officially opened to-day by Colonel Moore Brabazon, Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministry of Transport.

label: text
text:
This tube now runs from Edgware, north of London, through the centre of the capital to Morden, in the South, a distance of 21½ miles, and it is therefore the longest tube railway in the world.
Lord Ashfield, Chairman of the Underground Railways, in his speech mentioned that out of 125,000 invested in London transport, underground tubes represented £282,000,000.

label: text
text: The guests at the inaugura ceremony included a delegatio from German tube railways.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: BAR COUNCILS

label: text
text:
DIAN ASSEMBLY PASSES
NEW BILL.

label: text
text: The Assembly passed the Government Bill providing for the constitution of Bar Councils in the various Provinces of India.

label: text
text: the result of five n, and is the direct recommendations of appointed under the of Sir Edward

label: text
text: Sir Alexander Muddiman, moving for its consideration, pointed out that the Bill attempted the creation of a united Indian Bar by removing the distinctions which existed in the statue between Vakils and Barristers.

label: text
text: Barrister members, headed by Sir Harf Singh Gour, vigorously opposed the inclusion of two clauses which sought to deprive Barristers of their long enjoyed rights of seniority and pre-audience over Vakils in Indian High Courts. On the contrary, Vakil members considered that legal discriminations, existing either under the statute or by practice, were the essence of the Bar Committee's recommendations.

label: text
text:
The Home Member, Sir Alexander Muddiman, thereupon undertook, to consult the High Courts concerned regarding Barristers' seniority and pre-audience and bring an amending Bill if necessary. Opposition to the rest of the measure then subsided, though a few Barristers protested against any attempt to destroy the individuality of members of the English Bar, which contained the best traditions.
Before the Bill, as amended, passed the third reading, Sir Alexander Muddiman emphasised that success in working the Act depended on the goodwill and not on the Trade Union jealousy of those leading Barristers and Vakils who would man the various Councils.

label: paragraph_title
text: LANDSLIP IN BURMA

label: paragraph_title
text: OFFICIAL REPORT OF CASUALTIES.

label: text
text: Simla, August 28.

label: text
text: The Raj, in a communication regretting reports of the serious landslip at Tiger Camp, Bawdwin Minx, in the Northern Shan States, Burma, states that the landslip occurred on the evening of August 16, and devastated about seventy labourers' dwellings.

label: text
text: So far as is known at present twenty bodies have been recovered and 24 injured persons have been rescued. The rescue work is progressing under the guidance of an officer of the Mine Department.

text: Marshall Sun Chuan-fang is still stated to be inactive. From a reliable source it is gathered that the southerners are moving very slowly into Kiangsi, if at all, during the last two days. They seem to be waiting to see how things will pan out elsewhere.

label: text

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: Star in the Rear?

label: text
text: Fighting between rival Chinese armies continues in the neighbourhood of Hankow but Wuchang situated on the opposite bank of the Yangtze River to Hankow, is still holding out against the Cantonese forces of General Chang Kai-shek whose communications to the south are now rumoured to be threatened by troops of Marshal Sun Chuanfang.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: RECRUITS WANTED:

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, September 8.

label: text
text:
Several further troop movements took place yesterday but none were of a very important nature, and the "war" situation was more or less left in obscurity because of the excitement caused by the threat of the labourers and students (start "trouble yesterday, the occasion being the 25th anniversary of the signing of the Boxer Protocol).
Gen. Lu. Hsiang-ting, Tupan of Chekiang, has established in Shanghai a recruiting depot. The depot has been established in Nantao, near the Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway's south station, and the recruits are wanted for the training brigade.

label: text
text:
Searching on Railway.
Mr. C. P. Yin, managing director of the Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railways, has issued a notification to the effect that, acting on instructions from Marshal Sun Chuan-fang, military and police officers at the stations are searching all "incoming and outgoing passengers to see that they carry no arms or ammunition, contraband or Bolshevik literature. The public are warned to submit to these searches in order that there should be no unpleasantness and that peace and order may be preserved.

label: text
text: Special patrols are now being maintained by the Kianigsu Water Police, orders to this effect having been received from Marshal Sun Chuan-fang.—“N.-C. Daily News.”

label: paragraph_title
text: FOR THE FRONT.

label: text
text: Recruiting for the army of General Sun Chuan-fang, military overlord of the provinces of Klangsu, Kiangsi, Anhwei, Chekiang and Fukien, has started in Shanghai as General Sun drifts nearer and nearer to participation on the present conflict.

label: text
text: General Lu Hsiang-ting, who has been appointed by General Sun as Commander-in-Chief of his army, has sent his agents to recruit soldiers who will be sent to the front.

label: text
text: Starting on Sunday men are to be seen along Goong Hu Road and Dah Tung Road in Chapel with white banners in their hands which indicate their mission. At the terminus of North Chekiang Road, near a Chinese hotel, a big white flag was hoisted, which bore the letters, "Wanted Recruits."

label: paragraph_title
text: Still Hopeful.

label: text
text: That the whole present civil warfare affecting the provinces of Hunan and Hupeh amounts to anti-Red struggle is the contention of General Sun Chuan-fang as estimated to his officers and related to a local Chinese journalist recently at Shanghai.

label: text
text: General Sun is of the opinion that the motive which prompted the Allied troops to be engaged in a life-and-death fight is not one after private gains nor selfish ends, and for this simple reason he has sciemnly declared to adhere to Marshal Wu Pol-fu and render him assistance, both actual and constructive, whenever occasion demands.

label: text
text: However, General Sun still expresses the hope that the war will only be carried on in those two provinces, so that his territorial sovereignty along the Yangtze will not be encroached upon. Shanghai Times.

label: paragraph_title
text: SULTAN CAME BACK.

label: text
text: NATIVES THOUGHT HE WAS A CAPTIVE.

label: text
text: Paris, August 11.—Believing that Sultan Mulai Yusef of Morocco (who has recently been visiting Paris) had been enticed into captivity and that he would never return from France to his native country, the largest assemblage of Moors that has ever greeted a ruler awaited at Rabat (Morocco) to-day to make sure that it was really the Sultan who was returning to his palace and not a substitute.

label: text
text: Ever since the Sultan left for his tour of France a month ago wild reports had been spread around the native markets that he had walked into a trap and that the French would hold him as a hostage and might even banish him to some remote island.

label: text
text: Mountaineers from the Atlas country and from the Riff, and white robed tribesmen from the scrub and the desert welcomed him. It was a gathering that, for size and diversity, Morocco had never seen before.

label: paragraph_title
text: GREAT DECREASE IN POPULATION.

label: text
text: London, August 23.

label: text
text: Surprising figures are disclosed in the Irish Free State census in April. The population since 1911 has decreased by 167,000 to 2,972,000. During the same period the population of Northern Ireland has increased by nearly 6,000 to 1,256,322.

label: text
text: There are 973 females to every 1,000 males in the Free State and 1,066 females to each 1,000 males in Northern Ireland.—Times of Ceylon.

label: paragraph_title
text: PEKING'S STEP.

label: paragraph_title
text:
ENDING A CUSTOMS
TREATY.

label: text
text: The "China Express and Telegraph" writing on August 19 says:

label: text
text: It is reported from Geneva on August 17 that China has taken the first step towards the denunication of the so-called 'unequal' Customs Treaties, despite the negotiations at Peking by officially 'notifying Brussels that tariff pacts of extr-territoriality will automatically be terminated on October 29.

label: text
text: Commenting on this, the correspondent of the "Morning Post" says: The action of the special Chinese Tariff Commission carries out threats made recently by both the Chinese Minister at Rome and the Chinese Minister to the United States. According to official information received by Chinese diplomats at Geneva and throughout Europe, Peking is preparing to denounce all existing treaties three months before the extension period arrives. The Chinese have refused the request of the Powers for delay pending the outcome of additional pourparters. The abrogation of the Treaty with Belgium will be followed by similar action in regard to Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Italian, French, British, and American treaties.

label: text
text: The Chinese are now offering Belgium the opportunity to sign a complete Customs Treaty on lines of equality and reciprocity, similar to those between China and Austria and Germany. If she refuses, the Chinese will extend the boycott now aimed at the British and Japanese to various Belgian exports. According to Geneva authorities, Peking, despite the claim that China has no stable Government, is within its legal rights in repudiating Customs' extra-territorial treaties. Significantly, however, the Chinese are offering Belgium the same reciprocal treatment accorded to the Germans, thereby permitting importations at the same tariff as levied on most favoured nations. Although empowered to false tariffs on German goods, China is extending the lowest duties in order to encourage trade competition with Britain, Japan and America, and thereby forcing Customs revision.
